description:
Implement the additive NTT over GF($2^m$) — the missing transform that unlocks Reed–Solomon evaluation/interpolation workloads, binary-field proof-system workloads (FRI-Binius), and Frobenius-FFT-accelerated GF(2)[x] multiplication for code-based post-quantum cryptography.

## Background

The additive NTT [Lch2014] evaluates polynomials over an $\mathbb{F}_2$-linear subspace in the novel polynomial basis in $O(n \log n)$ field operations, replacing the multiplicative NTT that characteristic 2 lacks. Its original application is Reed–Solomon erasure coding, which makes an end-to-end RS workload — encoding, decoding, multipoint evaluation, and interpolation over transform lengths $n = 2^8$ through $2^{16}$ — the epic's primary empirical decision surface. The same transform is the core behind small-field polynomial commitment schemes over binary towers [DiamondPosen2023], the ring-switching FRI-Binius construction [DiamondPosen2024], and interleaved RAA-code SNARKs [Blaze2024]. The Frobenius additive FFT line applies the same machinery to GF(2)[x] multiplication at HQC/BIKE parameter sizes, where tuned carryless-multiply implementations currently set the bar [Jang2026]. The workspace already has tower-field arithmetic, Karatsuba multipliers, and SIMD kernel infrastructure (GFNI/VPCLMULQDQ paths); the transform itself is absent. One implementation pays into the RS, proof-system, and PQC benchmark directions.

A transform microbenchmark win alone does not settle the RS question: basis conversion, allocation, and composition with the surrounding pipeline can consume the asymptotic advantage. The RS criteria below therefore measure the full workload — encoding, decoding, multipoint evaluation, and interpolation separately — and compare three representation strategies — per-call basis conversion, conversion fused with an adjacent stage, and persistent novel-basis storage.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Forward and inverse additive NTT over GF($2^m$) in the novel polynomial basis, with property tests covering roundtrip identity and agreement with naive multipoint evaluation.
- [hard] REQ-02: A committed benchmark receipt measures NTT-based polynomial multiplication in GF($2^m$)[x] against the existing Karatsuba path across a predeclared degree range and records the measured crossover degree or its absence; the go/no-go decision for the NTT multiplication path is recorded either way.
- [hard] REQ-03: Benchmark comparison against a published binary-field NTT implementation (e.g. the binius-field crate), with methodology and results documented.
- [aspirational] REQ-04: SIMD-accelerated RAA (repeat–accumulate–accumulate) encoder demonstrating the interleaved-code commitment workload.
- [aspirational] REQ-05: Frobenius-FFT GF(2)[x] multiplication evaluated against carryless-multiply baselines at HQC parameter sizes.
- [hard] REQ-06: A predeclared end-to-end Reed–Solomon benchmark protocol names the primary throughput metric, the code rates and erasure/error model, the best existing baseline composition, two named CPU host classes, every transform length $n = 2^8, 2^9, \ldots, 2^{16}$, and the three basis-representation strategies (per-call conversion, fused conversion, persistent novel-basis storage); encoding, decoding, multipoint evaluation, and interpolation are four explicitly separate measurements, with allocation and basis conversion included in every measurement.
- [hard] REQ-07: A committed receipt executes the REQ-06 protocol on both host classes and records the go/no-go decision for additive-NTT RS against the REQ-08 thresholds, whichever way the measurements fall.
- [aspirational] REQ-08: Under the best representation strategy, the predeclared primary end-to-end RS metric from REQ-06 crosses over the baseline composition by $n \le 2^{14}$ and reaches at least $1.25\times$ the baseline at $n = 2^{16}$ with peak memory at most $2\times$ the baseline, on both host classes.

## References

- [Lch2014] Lin, Chung, Han — Novel Polynomial Basis and Its Application to Reed–Solomon Erasure Codes. FOCS 2014. arXiv:1404.3458.
- [DiamondPosen2023] Diamond, Posen — Succinct Arguments over Towers of Binary Fields (Binius). IACR eprint 2023/1784; EUROCRYPT 2025.
- [DiamondPosen2024] Diamond, Posen — Polylogarithmic Proofs for Multilinears over Binary Towers (ring switching / FRI-Binius). IACR eprint 2024/504.
- [Blaze2024] Brehm, Chen, Fisch, Resch, Rothblum, Zeilberger — Blaze: fast SNARKs from interleaved RAA codes over binary fields. IACR eprint 2024/1609; EUROCRYPT 2025.
- [Jang2026] Jang et al. — Optimized GF(2)[x] multiplication via VPCLMULQDQ/PMULL on HQC. J. Cryptographic Engineering (2026), doi:10.1007/s13389-026-00392-0.
title: Additive NTT over GF(2^m) for Reed–Solomon, proof-system, and PQC workloads
